dedupe_keys.name: mouse microreactor optimization using simulation and economics

description: MOUSE (Microreactor Optimization Using Simulation and Economics) is an open-source tool from Idaho National Laboratory that couples nuclear microreactor design with bottom-up economics for early technical and economic screening. It was developed by Botros Hanna, Chandrakanth Bolisetti and colleagues with sponsorship from the DOE Office of Nuclear Energy. It runs 2D OpenMC core models of liquid metal thermal, gas-cooled TRISO and heat pipe microreactors, adds simplified balance of plant calculations such as heat exchanger masses, pump power and building areas, and estimates preconstruction, direct, indirect, training, financial, operation and maintenance and fuel costs from MARVEL project data and literature, giving capital cost and levelised cost of energy for first and nth-of-a-kind units. The method is location-independent. It is Python code on GitHub under the MIT licence at no cost, released in July 2025, with a hosted Streamlit web app that needs no local OpenMC install. Caveats: cost data carry large uncertainty for first-of-a-kind plants and core models are 2D. Simulation uses are design and cost optimisation of microreactors for remote or resilient power.
